name: Pierre Auger Observatory

facility_roles.note: The Observatory facility and the experiment coincide; the observatory hosts and is the detector for this experiment.

intervals.label: collaboration formed / site selection
intervals.quote: A meeting is held in Paris to form the collaboration. It chooses the site of Mendoza, Argentina in the Southern Hemisphere.

intervals.label: international agreement signed
intervals.quote: Signature of the International Agreement in Mendoza.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Beginning of the construction of the observatory.

intervals.label: Engineering Array prototype
intervals.quote: The Engineering Array – a full-scale prototype of the first 32 SD stations and a single fluorescence telescope – is operated for 6 months.
intervals.note: Only the year is stated; the 6-month operating period's exact start/end months are not given.

intervals.label: data taking (partial then full array)
intervals.quote: First physics results are reported from more than 100 surface detector stations.
intervals.note: Physics data-taking began in 2004 with a partial array, years before the full 1660-station array and 27 fluorescence telescopes were completed (inaugurated November 2008); data taking has continued since.

intervals.label: AugerPrime upgrade
intervals.quote: As the commissioning of the final components of AugerPrime reaches its conclusion and the enhanced array comes fully online.
intervals.note: AugerPrime adds scintillator and radio detectors atop each existing water-Cherenkov station plus underground muon counters; the official history page dates the inaugurating symposium to November 2015, first SSD stations to September 2016, first radio-upgrade antenna to April 2019 and 'final completion of the RD deployment' to November 2024. The August 2025 status paper (arXiv:2508.08056) describes commissioning of the final components as 'reaching its conclusion' as of that writing; no fetched source gives an exact upgrade-complete date, so end is left open. Existing-array data taking continues throughout.

physics_goals.value: Determine the origin, mechanism and composition of the highest-energy cosmic rays, above 10^18 eV, using a hybrid surface-detector and fluorescence-telescope array too large for a single detector type to catch enough events.
physics_goals.quote: Cosmic rays with energies above 10^19 eV arrive on Earth at a rate of only 1 particle per square kilometer per year

physics_goals.value: Measure the ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray spectrum and search for the predicted GZK suppression of the flux above about 4x10^19 eV.
physics_goals.quote: Observation of the energy spectrum of cosmic rays confirmes that the flux is strongly suppressed above 4.10^19 eV as predicted by the GZK theory.

unique_capabilities.value: Hybrid detection: a 3000 km^2 surface array of water-Cherenkov tanks sampling shower particles at ground level, cross-calibrated against 27 fluorescence telescopes that image the longitudinal development of air showers on clear, dark nights.
unique_capabilities.quote: 3000 km2 array of 1660 particle detectors... overlooked by 27 optical telescopes

summary.plain: A giant hybrid detector in Argentina that catches the rarest, most energetic cosmic rays known: water tanks spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particle showers at ground level while telescopes watch the sky for their faint ultraviolet glow.
summary.technical: Hybrid ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory combining a 3000 km^2 surface array of 1660 water-Cherenkov detector stations with 27 fluorescence telescopes in Mendoza Province, Argentina. Proposed 1995, construction from 2000, partial-array data taking from 2004, full array inaugurated November 2008; currently undergoing the AugerPrime upgrade (scintillator, radio and underground-muon detectors added atop the existing water-Cherenkov stations) begun November 2015.

notes: site_ids, detector_ids, document_ids, result_ids are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1 derived fields).

status is 'upgrade' rather than 'active' because the AugerPrime upgrade interval (start 2015-11, open) is the most recently started interval covering the present per the A3 state-selection rule, even though existing-array data taking (interval started 2004) continues uninterrupted throughout the upgrade.
No results or technical documents were written in this pass (non-flagship experiment; mandatory bar only per the wave-3 brief).
